stemBlocks.value: A = (0  -1 / 1  0) represents a rotation of 90 degrees anticlockwise about the origin O, and B = (0  -1 / -1  0) represents a reflection in the line y = -x. (i) Write the coordinates of P', the image of P(7, 11) after a rotation of 90 degrees anticlockwise about O. (ii) T is the combined transformation A followed by B; determine the elements of the matrix representing T. (iii) Describe geometrically the transformation represented by T. (b) The matrix C = (3  k / 6  4) is singular; determine the value of k.
Think first: For a combined transformation, the matrix of the second transformation goes on the left, because it acts on the image the first one produced.

solutionSteps.instruction: Multiply A by the position vector of P.
For A followed by B, write the combined matrix as BA, not AB.

contentBlocks.value: The point is first multiplied by A, then that result is multiplied by B: B(A x) = (BA)x.

solutionSteps.instruction: Apply T to a general point to describe it.

contentBlocks.value: (-1  0 / 0  1)(x / y) = (-x / y): the x-coordinate changes sign and the y-coordinate is unchanged.
Result: T is a reflection in the y-axis (the line x = 0)

solutionSteps.instruction: For (b), a singular matrix has determinant zero.

strategyBlocks.value: Multiply A by the column vector for P, form the product BA for the combined transformation, read off the geometric effect of that matrix on a general point, then set det C = 0 for part (b).

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) P'(-11, 7)  (ii) T = (-1  0 / 0  1)  (iii) T is a reflection in the y-axis, the line x = 0.  (b) k = 2

whyThisWorks.value: A transformation matrix acts on the left of a column vector, so applying A and then B gives B(Ax), which by associativity equals (BA)x; the matrix of a combined transformation is therefore the product with the second transformation written first. Reading the columns of a 2x2 transformation matrix tells you where (1, 0) and (0, 1) go, which pins the transformation down completely. A matrix is singular when its determinant is zero, because then it has no inverse and cannot be undone.

commonErrors.misconception: Computing AB instead of BA and getting (1  0 / 0  -1), a reflection in the x-axis.
